name: Tape
description: What tape does to a sound: saturation that dulls loud highs, wow and flutter, head bump, the bandwidth of the chosen speed, and the dropouts and hiss of a worn reel.

params.name: Drive
params.description: How hard the signal hits the tape. More adds harmonics and squashes peaks, and loud passages lose their treble first.

params.name: Wow
params.description: Slow pitch drift that wanders and never quite repeats. Zero is a steady transport.

params.name: Flutter
params.description: Fast, fine pitch wobble that makes held notes tremble. Zero is a steady transport.

params.name: Speed
params.description: Which machine and tape speed. Slower speeds are darker and hissier, with a slower wobble and a higher head bump. Cassette is the dullest.

params.name: Age
params.description: How worn the tape is. More age dulls the top, deepens the wow and flutter, and brings dropouts, brief dips in level.

params.name: Hiss
params.description: Level of tape noise. It sounds only while signal is passing and for a moment after, so silence stays silent.

params.name: Head Bump
params.description: The low-end lift of the playback head. Where it sits depends on Speed: lower on fast tape, higher on cassette.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Brightness of the playback. Low rolls off more of the top; high opens it beyond what the chosen speed gives.

params.name: Output
params.description: Volume of the taped signal, set after the saturation and before Mix. The dry signal is not affected.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the tape sound.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A behavioural sketch of a tape machine (emphasis around a soft saturator, a wobbling transport, playback equalisation per speed, dropouts, hiss), not a model of any one deck or of magnetic hysteresis. Hiss is only made while the device is awake: it carries on for a second after the input stops, fades, and an idle track is exactly silent.
